text: Databases are essential tools for storing and organizing information. The most common type is the relational database, which uses tables made up of rows and columns. To interact with these tables, we use SQL (Structured Query Language), a standard language for writing queries that retrieve, insert, or update data. Before building a database, careful data modeling is required to define the relationships between different pieces of information, ensuring efficiency and accuracy. To speed up searches, developers create indexes on specific columns, allowing the database to find data quickly without scanning every row. Alternatively, NoSQL databases, like MongoDB, store data in flexible documents instead of rigid tables. They are useful for projects with changing data structures or massive amounts of unstructured information, offering scalability at the cost of some consistency.
